title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: directors, officers and employees (including regular consultants)
tiers.description: The single tier to which the whole Policy applies. Officers include directors, secretaries and other persons who manage the Company. All substantive prohibitions (blackout periods, the ban on derivatives and hedging over unvested Securities, prior notification and trade confirmation) apply uniformly to this tier; the Policy does not create separate KMP, PDMR or restricted-person categories.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Directors of Ramelius. Distinguished only by the requirement, under undertakings entered into with the Company, to advise their interests in Ramelius Securities on appointment, on every change and on retirement, so the Company can notify ASX under Listing Rules 3.19A.1 to 3.19A.3 no later than three business days after the relevant date.

tiers.name: the Chairman
tiers.description: The Chairman, who cannot self-clear: he must complete Part A of a Trade Notification Form and obtain Part B from the Managing Director, and it is the Managing Director who exercises the exceptional-circumstances discretion for him.

tiers.name: immediate family and controlled entities
tiers.description: Immediate family and companies, trusts or other entities over which the director, officer, employee or regular consultant, or an immediate family member, has control. Personnel must take reasonable steps to prohibit dealing in the Company's Securities by them.

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board of Directors may determine that a prohibition on dealing should apply, notified to directors, officers and employees by the Chairman, Managing Director or Company Secretary by email or other written means. The Board may also amend the Policy and extend or shorten a permitted period at any time, with notice by email or other written means. The Policy says nothing about whether the reason for a prohibition is confidential.

rules.section: The Company's Trading Policy (b) Specific Prohibition
rules.detail: A flat ban, with no approval route and no venue distinction, on using derivatives in relation to unvested Ramelius Securities. It is expressed together with hedging arrangements and applies to all directors, officers, employees and regular consultants.
rules.evidence: Directors, officers and employees (including regular consultants) must also not use derivatives and hedging arrangements in relation to unvested Ramelius Securities.

rules.section: Insider Trading (definition of the Company's Securities); (b); (d)
rules.detail: The express derivatives ban reaches only unvested Securities. For vested Securities a derivative is caught by the definition of the Company's Securities, which expressly includes any financial or associated product issued or created over the Company's Securities by third parties, with no venue limitation on that limb. Dealing therefore requires a completed Trade Notification Form with Part B signed by the Chairman (or the Managing Director for the Chairman), must fall outside the blackout periods, and must be confirmed to the Company Secretary afterwards.
rules.evidence: The Company's Securities means shares, options or other financial products issued by Ramelius that are traded on the Australian Securities Exchange Limited (“ASX”) and include any financial or associated product issued or created over the Company's Securities by third parties.

rules.detail: Hedging arrangements in relation to unvested Ramelius Securities are prohibited outright. Hedging is not defined, so the scope of what constitutes a hedging arrangement is left open, and there is no discretion to permit it.
rules.evidence: must also not use derivatives and hedging arrangements in relation to unvested Ramelius Securities

rules.detail: The prohibition is keyed to Securities being unvested. The Policy says nothing about Securities that have vested but remain subject to a holding lock or disposal restriction, so such shares are not caught by the express ban, though the plan rules (not incorporated) may restrict them.

Hedging vested Ramelius Securities is not prohibited. The hedging instrument is itself a financial or associated product created over the Company's Securities and so a Security, meaning the prior notification, blackout and trade confirmation requirements apply but no substantive prohibition does.
rules.evidence: Directors, officers and employees (including regular consultants) must not deal in Ramelius Securities without first completing Part A of a Notification to Trade in Ramelius Securities Form

rules.detail: Monetisation, prepaid forwards and similar structures are not named. Each involves a financial or associated product created over the Company's Securities and an agreement to dispose of Securities, both of which are caught, so prior notification and Chairman sign-off are required and the transaction cannot be entered into during a blackout period.
rules.evidence: trade or deal in (i.e. apply for, acquire or dispose) the Company's Securities or enter into an agreement to trade in the Company's Securities

rules.detail: Short selling is not mentioned anywhere in the Policy and there is no economic-effect or downside-position test.
Securities lending is not mentioned and the trading definitions cover only applying for, acquiring or disposing of Securities and agreements to do so.

CFDs are not named. A CFD over Ramelius shares is a financial or associated product created over the Company's Securities by a third party and so falls within the Policy, requiring prior notification and Chairman sign-off; over unvested Securities it would be a prohibited derivative.
rules.evidence: include any financial or associated product issued or created over the Company's Securities by third parties

rules.detail: Margin lending, margin calls and forced sales by a financier are not mentioned anywhere in this 2011 policy. There is no prohibition, no approval requirement and no disclosure obligation attaching to a margin loan as such.

Granting security, a charge, lien or pledge over Ramelius Securities is not addressed. The trading definitions extend only to applying for, acquiring or disposing of Securities and to agreements to do so, so the grant of security is not on its face a trade requiring notification, although the eventual enforcement sale would be a disposal.

There is no secured financing clause of any kind: no prohibition, no threshold, no disclosure of financing arrangements, no LVR or trigger guidance, and no treatment of a lender's unilateral sale rights.
The Policy contains no short-term or speculative trading restriction, no minimum holding period and no intention test.

clearance.tier: directors, officers and employees (including regular consultants)
clearance.approver: The Chairman completes Part B of the Trade Notification Form (the Managing Director does so for the Chairman). Although Part B is stated not to be an approval, the Chairman may direct that the trade should not be undertaken and the person must comply.
clearance.post_trade_to: Company Secretary, by a Confirmation of Trade in Ramelius Securities Form
clearance.post_trade_deadline: unspecified ("when a trade in the Company's Securities has occurred")
clearance.evidence: Notification of any trade and completion of Part B of a Trade Notification Form does not constitute approval by or on behalf of Ramelius for the relevant trade. ... the Chairman ... must ... either; complete Part B of the Trade Notification Form; or direct the director/officer/employee that the trade should not be undertaken. A director/officer/employee must comply with the direction given.

clearance.approver: The Chairman (the Managing Director for the Chairman)
clearance.post_trade_to: Company Secretary (Trade Confirmation Form); and the Company, with details of all changes in the director's interests, for onward notification to ASX under Listing Rule 3.19A.2
clearance.post_trade_deadline: as soon as possible after the date of the change in interests and in any event no later than three business days after that date
clearance.evidence: Directors must provide details of their directors' interests in Ramelius Securities as soon as possible after ... date of the change in their interests ... and in any event, no later than three business days after the relevant date.

exceptions.approver: The Chairman (or the Managing Director in the case of the Chairman), exercisable only before the trade
exceptions.evidence: If there are exceptional circumstances (such as a pressing financial commitment or hardship) and a director, officer or employee declares their special circumstances and that they are not in possession of any insider information via a Trade Notification Form, the Chairman ... may exercise a discretion to allow the director, officer or employee to trade in the Company's Securities outside a permitted period

Permitted periods for dealing in the Company's Securities may include any period during which a pro-rata issue or other entitlement is generally open to Ramelius shareholders to enable directors, officers and employees (including regular consultants) that are shareholders to deal with the entitlement on offer.

external_documents: Undertakings entered into by directors with Ramelius in respect of notification of their interests in Ramelius Securities
Employee incentive plan rules governing unvested Ramelius Securities (referred to only through the term 'unvested', not reproduced)
exemption_authority: The Chairman, or the Managing Director in the case of the Chairman, may exercise a discretion to allow a trade outside a permitted period where the person declares exceptional circumstances (such as a pressing financial commitment or hardship) and that they hold no inside information, via a Trade Notification Form. The discretion may only be exercised before the trade and not after the event, and the trade remains subject to paragraphs (a), (b) and (d) to (f), so it cannot cure the ban on derivatives and hedging over unvested Securities.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors, officers and employees (including regular consultants) must also not use derivatives and hedging arrangements in relation to unvested Ramelius Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is the only substantive obstacle to a collar: it bites only on unvested Securities, so a collar over fully vested shares is not prohibited, but the collared parcel must be strictly segregated from any unvested performance rights or options.

bespoke_clauses.topic: notification is not approval but carries a veto
bespoke_clauses.clause: Notification of any trade and completion of Part B of a Trade Notification Form does not constitute approval by or on behalf of Ramelius for the relevant trade. ... the Chairman ... must ... either complete Part B ... or direct the director/officer/employee that the trade should not be undertaken. A director/officer/employee must comply with the direction given.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank gets no company approval it can rely on, but the Chairman holds an unqualified veto with no criteria, no response deadline and no stated validity period for a completed Part B, so timing risk on pricing the collar sits with the executive.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Policy contains no reference to margin loans, margin calls, security interests, encumbrances, forced sales, short selling, securities lending or short-term trading.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar is unregulated by this policy, but that silence cuts both ways: there is no framework permitting or disclosing the financing and no protection against the bank's enforcement sale falling in a blackout period, so the position should be documented with the Chairman up front.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Company's Securities ... include any financial or associated product issued or created over the Company's Securities by third parties.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A bank-issued OTC put and call over Ramelius shares are the Company's Securities for Policy purposes, so entering into, and later unwinding, each leg is a trade needing a Trade Notification Form and Chairman sign-off outside a blackout.

bespoke_clauses.topic: frequent blackouts for a quarterly reporter
bespoke_clauses.clause: during the period between the end of the Company's full financial year and the announcement of the Company's full year financial results ... during the period between the end of the Company's half year and the announcement of the Company's half year financial results ... during the one week period immediately prior to the lodgement of the Company's quarterly activity reports.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The full-year and half-year blackouts run from period end to results announcement, which can be six to eight weeks each, and every quarterly report adds a further week, materially narrowing the dates on which a collar can be struck or rolled.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the Board of Directors may determine that there are specific periods when directors, officers and employees are permitted to deal ... The Board of Directors may from time to time amend this trading policy or may extend or shorten a permitted period for dealing.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Dealing windows are defined by Board determination rather than by fixed anchors and can be shortened at will, so a scheduled roll or unwind of the collar can be blocked at short notice.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The discretion may only be exercised before a trade in the Company's Securities and not after the event.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: If the bank enforces its security or the collar physically settles during a prohibited period, the breach cannot be cured retrospectively, so settlement mechanics must be conditioned on prior notification.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors, officers, employees (including regular consultants) must take reasonable steps to prohibit dealing in the Company's Securities by immediate family and companies, trusts or other entities over which the director, officer, employee and regular consultant or immediate family member has control.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Booking the collar through a family trust or controlled company does not avoid the Policy, and the obligation is framed as taking reasonable steps to prohibit their dealing altogether.

summary: A funded collar over fully vested Ramelius shares is possible under this policy, which is short, dated December 2011, and silent on financing. The only substantive prohibition relevant to the structure is that derivatives and hedging arrangements must not be used in relation to unvested Ramelius Securities, so the collared parcel must consist solely of vested shares. Both option legs are nevertheless the Company's Securities, because the definition expressly includes any financial or associated product issued or created over those Securities by third parties, so entry, roll and unwind each require a Trade Notification Form with Part B signed by the Chairman (the Managing Director for the Chairman) and a Trade Confirmation Form to the Company Secretary, and must avoid the blackout from each period end to the results announcement, the week before each quarterly activity report, and any Board-determined prohibition. Part B is expressly not an approval, yet the Chairman can direct that a trade not be undertaken, so the bank obtains no reliance from the process. Margin lending, security interests, forced sales and short selling are entirely unaddressed, meaning the loan leg is not prohibited but also carries no agreed treatment for enforcement during a blackout, and the discretion to permit an out-of-window trade cannot be exercised after the event.
